key_insight: This review traces how automated materials information extraction has evolved from rule-based pipelines to LLMs and agentic systems spanning text, tables, and figures.
engineering_relevance: Literature-derived databases and knowledge graphs can support materials discovery, research assistance, and closed-loop optimization when integrated with autonomous laboratories.
method: Review rule-based, NLP, transformer-encoder, and LLM extraction approaches.
Assess generated datasets, extraction accuracy, computational costs, and methodological trade-offs.
Outline practical guidance for reliable, scalable extraction pipelines.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a critical assessment of datasets, accuracy, and costs, but reports no quantitative results and highlights a shortage of reliable benchmarks.
watch_item: Reliably linking structure, properties, processing, and performance for individual samples remains an open challenge, compounded by inconsistent terminology across document modalities.
paper_title: Automated Materials Data and Knowledge Extraction using Machine Learning and Large Language Models
